newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks to make its market more people friendly.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks to make its market more people friendly.

text.p: The European Union will on Tuesday launch an information campaign aimed at making the 15-nation bloc's border-free market more comprehensible and user-friendly for its 370 million citizens.

At a special ceremony at the European Parliament at 1200 GMT Commission President Jacques Santer, single market commissioner Mario Monti, and a host of ministers and parliamentarians will launch a campaign dubbed "citizens first," the Commission said on Monday.

The open market where goods, people, services and capital should have been able to move freely from January 1, 1993, has often been criticised for being business-oriented and for ignoring the ordinary man and woman on the street.
But the European Commission has argued that ordinary citizens often do not make use of it because they are unaware of what it can do for them as it has been badly explained.
The campaign will operate through brochures, television spots, phone lines and a web site on the Internet.

It will try to explain to people exactly how they can live, work and study in other parts of the Union, how they can benefit from EU rules on equal opportunities and how they can claim compensation for faulty goods bought in another country.
